paragraphs: Caution signal | This page corresponds to O*NET-SOC 25-9031.00 "Instructional Coordinators". The official scope is: develop instructional material, coordinate educational content, and incorporate current technology into instruction in order to provide guidelines to educators and instructors for developing curricula and conducting courses; may train and coach teachers; includes educational consultants and specialists, and instructional material directors. The occupation is not flagged Bright Outlook. The core deliverable is curriculum and instruction improvement plans, not "teaching a good lesson" itself. Risks come from insufficient curriculum and standards basis, incomplete teacher evaluation evidence, out-of-authority material procurement, and improper handling of student data and personal information. US wages and employment are the precise-occupation BLS definition presented by O*NET (median annual wage 77,440 USD; 2024 employment about 232,600 people, 2024—2034 growth below average 1%—2%, projected average annual openings about 21,900; main industry educational services). If you find it hard to bear multi-party coordination, long hours, and results that depend on others to execute, you should weigh these as real costs needing serious consideration.

Assume judgment | Real fit comes from whether you can accomplish three things at once in the same job: make curriculum and instruction solid (analyze curriculum and standards, design instructional materials and training, observe and give feedback, evaluate and iterate, and produce reviewable curriculum plans and instruction records); keep standards and compliance under control (curriculum standards and regulatory basis, teacher evaluation evidence and procedures, material procurement and budget authority, student data and personal information boundaries, executed per agency and regulations); and carry definable job responsibilities (be accountable for your own curriculum plans and recommendations, and request or hand off curriculum standard interpretations, evaluation conclusions, and procurement approvals per process). It is suggested to test with one verifiable experience (complete a fully fictional curriculum improvement plan and training plan) rather than relying only on the conclusions of an interest questionnaire.

To judge whether you fit instructional coordination, first run a verifiable exercise with public or simulated material: set up a fully fictional instruction improvement scenario (for example, doing unit design for a batch of fictional courses), write out the process from analyzing curriculum standards and needs, designing instructional materials and activities, planning teacher training, observation and feedback, evaluating learning outcomes, to iteration and retrospective, and mark the checkpoints and possible problems at each step (insufficient curriculum and standards basis, incomplete or procedurally improper teacher evaluation evidence, out-of-authority material procurement, improper handling of student data or personal information, implementation drift because results depend on others to execute). After completing it, check: whether curriculum standards, evaluation procedures, procurement authority, and data boundaries are treated as non-omittable items; whether curriculum standard interpretations or evaluation conclusions beyond your personal authority are written as requests or handoffs; whether the process is left as reviewable records. All material must be fictional; do not use real student or teacher evaluation data.

Fit signal | The work activities of O*NET 25-9031.00 are mainly establishing and maintaining interpersonal relationships, communicating with supervisors and peers, organizing and prioritizing, training and teaching others, using computers, and making decisions and solving problems. If you are willing to continuously coordinate around curriculum standards, instructional materials, and teacher development, can accurately record the basis, process, and evaluation, and can push forward steadily under multiple demands and compliance constraints, these daily requirements are closer to your way of working; interest and personality tools are only for designing experiments and cannot judge hiring eligibility or performance.

Instructional coordinators correspond to US O*NET-SOC 25-9031.00 "Instructional Coordinators". The official scope is: develop instructional material, coordinate educational content, and incorporate current technology into instruction to provide guidelines to educators and instructors for developing curricula and conducting courses; may train and coach teachers; includes educational consultants and specialists, and instructional material directors. The typical work loop is analyzing curriculum standards and needs, designing instructional materials and training, observation and feedback, evaluation and iteration, and retrospective and recording. US wages and employment on this page use the precise-occupation BLS 25-9031.00 definition presented by O*NET (2025 median annual wage 77,440 USD; 2025 employment about 248,700 people, 2025—2035 growth below average 1%—2%, projected average annual openings about 23,100; main industry educational services); the O*NET summary page does not list the 10/25/75/90 percentiles, and this page does not publish them; precise wages for this occupation in mainland China were not obtained and are registered as a visible gap.

entries: Input objects | The objects are curriculum standards and syllabi, instructional materials and activities, teacher development and training, and assessment and student data; execute design and coordination within authorization and education policy boundaries.

Checkable outputs | Reviewable curriculum and unit plans, instructional material and activity designs, teacher training plans and records, observation and feedback records, and evaluation and iteration conclusions; results must be traceable to curriculum standards, the basis, and procedures.
Complete workflow | Analyze curriculum standards and needs → design instructional materials and training → observe and give feedback → evaluate and iterate → retrospective and recording.

paragraphs: Key judgments | O*NET work context shows: email 100% daily, indoors, environmentally controlled 100% daily, face-to-face discussions 95% daily, continual contact with others 83%, work with others in a group or team 82% extremely important, coordinating or leading others 61% extremely important. The basis for judgment is curriculum standards and regulatory basis, teacher evaluation evidence and procedures, and the authorization and compliance requirements for material procurement and student data.

Environment and pace | The work is mainly planning, communication, training, and recording: work week over 40 hours 94%, decision freedom 50% a lot of freedom, responsibility for others' work outcomes 50% high responsibility, time pressure 54% once a month or more but not every week. The pace is driven by the school year and project cycles, and results require others to execute to take effect.

Research inputs | O*NET 25-9031.00 provides the precise occupational identity, tasks, work context, and skills; the interest code is SEI (social—enterprising—investigative), Job Zone Five (60% require a master's degree, 25% a bachelor's degree, 11% a post-master's certificate), and it is not flagged Bright Outlook. Available US data are the precise-occupation BLS definition presented by O*NET: 2025 median annual wage 77,440 USD (median hourly 37.23); 2025 employment about 248,700 people, 2025—2035 growth below average (1%—2%), projected average annual openings about 23,100; main industry educational services. The O*NET summary page does not list the 10/25/75/90 percentiles; fields that were not opened or not published cannot be inferred from occupational identity.

What this job first checks: objects (curriculum standards and syllabi, instructional materials, teacher training, assessment and student data), inputs (curriculum standards and regulatory basis, learner and teacher needs, evaluation procedures, procurement and budget authority), deliverables (curriculum and unit plans, training plans and records, observation feedback, evaluation and iteration conclusions). If any item is unverified it should be treated as pending verification; experience or proxy measures cannot replace curriculum standards and procedures.

To judge the work loop, look at four steps: input check (confirm curriculum standards, needs, and authorization boundaries) → task limitation (proceed only within the approved curriculum and evaluation procedures) → execute and record (complete design, training, and observation records to standard) → review and escalation (stop immediately and report insufficient basis, evaluation disputes, and out-of-authority decisions). The loop holds only when the basis and procedures are verifiable, not merely whether the curriculum was delivered on schedule.

Adjacent responsibility boundaries | This page covers only the precise occupation O*NET-SOC 25-9031.00 "Instructional Coordinators". Adjacent occupations such as training and development managers, education administrators, kindergarten through secondary, training and development specialists, educational, guidance, and career counselors and advisors, and postsecondary teachers differ in work objects, authorization scope, and responsibility boundaries; they cannot be interchanged by job title alone, and proxy measures cannot replace agency authorization, licenses, and final responsibility.

entries.entity: Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors

paragraphs: Training and development managers direction | The core output is the organization's training system, budget, and team management. This occupation focuses on curriculum and instruction coordination; the management scope and assessment objects differ, and sharing training skills does not mean the responsibility is the same.

Education administrators, kindergarten through secondary direction | The core output is school operations, teacher management, and education policy execution. This occupation focuses on curriculum and instruction design; the authorization level and administrative responsibility differ, so it cannot be interchanged by job title alone.

Training and development specialists direction | The core output is the design and delivery of employee-facing training programs. This occupation focuses more on curriculum standards, curriculum systems, and teacher development; the objects, compliance requirements, and outcome definitions differ and must be checked separately.

Educational, guidance, and career counselors and advisors direction | The core output is learner-facing guidance, counseling, and academic and career advice. This occupation focuses on curriculum and instruction improvement; the service recipients and confidentiality and licensing requirements differ and cannot be applied to each other.
The work objects of instructional coordinators and the AI boundary: which steps may be assisted and which judgments must be borne by people.

Direct answer | Generative AI can assist with organizing curriculum standard points, generating drafts of instructional materials and activities, designing practice items and assessment drafts, and summarizing teacher feedback and observation records, but curriculum standard interpretation, evaluation conclusions, teacher coaching judgments, procurement and budget decisions, and compliant handling of student data still rest with people. Task exposure does not equal job substitution, nor does it mean it is already widely adopted; formal use requires authorization, human review, and documentation. This page gives no substitution probability or timeline. AI Impact Score 50% is an editorial estimate. Model impact index for three equally weighted representative core tasks; not a measured share of working time or a job-loss probability. floor((50+75+25)/3+0.5)=50; fermatmind-ai-impact-v1; 2026-10-18.The three tasks, ratings and sources are listed in the FermatMind method source record on this page.

Evidence note | This table uses only the original source definitions: O*NET 25-9031.00 provides the precise occupational identity, tasks, work context, and skills; US wages and employment use the precise-occupation BLS definition presented by O*NET; internal task specifications are used only for task breakdown and responsibility boundaries and do not measure adoption rates; the National Bureau of Statistics publishes average wages by industry category and cannot replace precise wages for this occupation.

Difference note | Within the same occupation, different steps are affected differently: the more text-based and post-verifiable the part (material and activity drafts, practice items, feedback summaries), the more it can be a candidate for trial tools, and actual efficiency needs to be verified with samples from this position; the more it involves curriculum standard interpretation, evaluation conclusions, teacher coaching, and data compliance, the more it must rest with people.

Responsibility chain | From curriculum standard and basis confirmation, tool processing, human review, evaluation and procurement approval, to record keeping, each step must specify who is responsible and retain traceable evidence; decisions affecting curriculum recognition, evaluation conclusions, and procurement must not rely on the model alone.

Turning point | Editorial judgment: tools may assist the efficiency of generating materials and drafts, but do not change where curriculum standard interpretation, evaluation judgment, teacher coaching, and data compliance responsibility lies; the pragmatic approach is to first build solid curriculum design, evaluation, and teacher development skills, then introduce tools in reviewable, traceable, low-risk steps.

May be assisted: organizing curriculum standard points, drafts of instructional materials and activities, practice items and assessment drafts, and summarizing teacher feedback; these steps' results can be checked afterward, but the curriculum standards, basis, and original records must still be revisited.

Human control points: you must go back to the original data and basis and review key judgments, and bear responsibility for curriculum standard interpretation, evaluation conclusions, teacher coaching, and student data compliance.

Occupation name comparison | Instructional coordinators correspond to US O*NET-SOC 25-9031.00; the National Bureau of Statistics urban unit wage releases consulted here are grouped by industry and broad occupation and cannot be used to establish a China equivalent wage distribution for this occupation.

Broad definition reference | Instructional curriculum and teacher development duties relate to the education industry. National Bureau of Statistics tables 2 and 5: 2025 average annual wages of employed persons in China's urban education industry units, non-private units 133,539 yuan and private units 63,908 yuan; the two statistical populations are listed separately and are not the wage range, median, or take-home income of instructional coordinators.

Insufficient evidence: mainland China public occupational statistics have not established a national occupational wage distribution for instructional coordinators precisely corresponding to US O*NET-SOC 25-9031.00; the National Bureau of Statistics publishes average wages by industry category and does not distinguish occupations, and this page does not substitute industry averages, job postings, or US data.

AI and wage boundary | Material drafts and feedback organization can be trial candidates for tools. Insufficient evidence: no occupation-level data on AI adoption, actual efficiency, or wage causal effects for instructional coordinators were obtained; this page does not infer individual wages from task exposure.
US wage reference | BLS data presented by O*NET (2025), on the precise-occupation definition for 25-9031.00.

US wages and employment | The 2025 annual wages at the 10/25/50/75/90 percentiles are 47,980 / 60,780 / 77,440 / 98,820 / 121,670 USD respectively. The national wage page has been checked; percentiles are not starting pay or experience levels. 2025 employment 248,700 people, 2025—2035 growth 2%, average annual openings 23,100 (including growth and replacement). Source: https://www.onetonline.org/link/localwages/25-9031.00.

Wage definition | The data are BLS OEWS 2025 and the 2025—2035 employment projection, presented by O*NET on the precise-occupation definition for 25-9031.00; OEWS is employer-reported wages including commissions and production bonuses, excluding overtime premiums, nonproduction bonuses, and employer benefit costs; percentiles are statistical positions and do not equal starting pay or individual take-home income.

Interpretation note | This definition can be used to understand the wage magnitude and demand direction of this occupation; it cannot serve as an individual quote, nor can it be compared directly with mainland China or any other market.

Industry wage reference | 2025 US median annual wages for this occupation by industry: Government (excluding state and local education and hospitals) 89,920 USD; local public elementary and secondary schools 82,130 USD; private colleges, universities, and professional schools 73,070 USD; private education support services 72,610 USD. Only the industries corresponding to the official sub-tables are shown; industry distribution, wages, and annual openings are explained separately. Source: https://www.bls.gov/ooh/education-training-and-library/instructional-coordinators.htm.

Influencing factors | Employer type (public, private, school district, training institution), region, education and seniority, and the scope of duties affect actual income level and stability; the median on this page is a statistical position and does not correspond to specific years of experience.

To work as an instructional coordinator, which interests, abilities, and ways of working matter more? This page discusses fit only with work samples and responsibility boundaries, and does not use personality labels to replace judgments of eligibility and performance.

Direct answer | The fit signal is whether you can steadily complete design, training, observation, and evaluation around curriculum standards and instructional materials, and escalate when the basis is insufficient or parties conflict — not a personality label. Interest and personality tools can only help design experiments and cannot judge hiring eligibility, authorization, or performance.

Positive signals | Able to complete curriculum and unit design, teacher training, and observation records to standard; able to check curriculum standards and evaluation basis and identify deviations; able to leave the process and conclusions as reviewable records and hand off accurately within authorization and compliance boundaries.

Caution conditions | Risk signals include drawing conclusions when the curriculum standard basis is insufficient, incomplete teacher evaluation evidence or improper procedures, out-of-authority material procurement, improper handling of student data or personal information, or being unwilling to report conflicts up the authorization chain; if you find it hard to bear multi-party coordination, long hours, and results that depend on others to execute, you should weigh these as real costs needing serious consideration.

Trial action | Run an exercise with a fully fictional instruction improvement scenario: write a unit design and instructional materials, plan a teacher training session, and design observation and evaluation records; test with observable deliverables rather than an interest questionnaire alone.

Conclusion | Activity preference is closer to a combination of helping and teaching, organizing and leading, and research and investigation (O*NET interest code SEI); but an interest code can only help design experiments and cannot judge hiring eligibility or performance.

Personality tool boundary | This page provides no validation evidence that personality tests predict instructional coordinator performance. It is suggested to observe curriculum standard checking, teacher feedback, and collaboration records; these are editorial suggestions, not conclusions about relative personality validity.

Conclusion | RIASEC or personality frameworks can only help raise questions and cannot replace work samples, learning ability, qualifications, and actual performance evidence for this occupation; no tool conclusion constitutes a hiring, authorization, or appointment decision.

Curriculum standard basis risk | Trigger: insufficient curriculum and standards basis, unclear version or applicable audience. Consequences: may cause instructional direction deviation and wasted resources. Control: check curriculum standards and regulatory basis, retain the basis and version, and stop and escalate on exceptions. Boundary: curriculum standard interpretation is determined per agency and competent-authority requirements.

Teacher evaluation and coaching risk | Trigger: incomplete evaluation evidence, improper procedures, or making an evaluation conclusion beyond authority. Consequences: may cause unfair evaluation and labor and personnel risk. Control: collect evidence per procedure, distinguish fact from inference, and conclusions must be authorized and documented. Boundary: personnel and evaluation conclusions are made by authorized personnel per agency rules.

Procurement and budget risk | Trigger: material, equipment, or service procurement beyond authority or with noncompliant procedures. Consequences: may cause compliance risk and resource loss. Control: execute per procurement and budget procedures and retain comparison and approval records. Boundary: procurement and budget approvals are made by authorized personnel per agency rules.

Student data and privacy risk | Trigger: student learning data, evaluation records, or personal information processed or sent outside the authorized scope. Consequences: may cause compliance risk and harm to rights. Control: process per minimum necessity and the authorized scope, keep processing and sharing records. Boundary: decisions affecting delivery or compliance must not rely on the model alone.

Common escalation rules | Once curriculum standards, evaluation procedures, or authorization conditions are insufficient, stop the related steps first and hand off the facts, impact, and open questions as reviewable records to the responsible person with authority; do not go past regulations, professional opinions, or organizational authorization, and do not use model output to replace agency authorization and final responsibility.

How to become an instructional coordinator: entry preparation, training, and responsibility path. Entry preparation should start with understanding curriculum standards, instructional design, and teacher development; specific training and employment requirements are determined by employers or competent authorities, and courses and certificates do not automatically grant teaching, evaluation, or management authority.

US entry | The typical entry-level education in BLS OOH is a master's degree, with related experience of five years or more; common experience comes from teaching or school administration. O*NET Job Zone Five describes the occupational preparation level, and the education distribution is survey information, not a uniform threshold for all employers. Public school positions may require a state-issued license, to be checked with the state education department; China positions are checked separately for recruitment conditions and qualifications.

Specific jurisdiction requirements | The US side uses O*NET preparation information to represent the typical path together with position practice; teacher qualifications, job entry, and education management requirements in mainland China are governed by relevant regulations and agency rules and must be checked separately, not applied to each other.

Qualification boundary | Courses or certificates do not automatically grant teaching, evaluation, or management authority for this occupation; education, certificates, licenses (where applicable), hiring, agency authorization, and evaluation authority are different states, and specific requirements depend on the position and applicable rules.

Stage responsibility | In the entry and trial stages, complete material design, training, and observation records under supervision; in later stages, independently complete curriculum and evaluation plans per position authorization and be accountable for the basis, procedures, and conclusions.

Reviewable evidence | Demonstrate ability with a fully fictional instruction improvement scenario: curriculum and unit plans, instructional materials, teacher training plans, and observation and evaluation records; do not use real student or teacher evaluation data, and note the basis and assumptions.

Next action | Complete one fictional curriculum plan and training plan, ask an experienced person to challenge your curriculum standard judgments, evaluation procedures, and data boundaries, and use that to judge whether to keep investing in this direction; prove ability with observable deliverables rather than course names.

Transition path | Before transitioning, first list transferable abilities (curriculum and instruction analysis, instructional design and training, observation and evaluation, coordination and communication, recording and documentation), then clarify the new position's tools, qualifications, and responsibility evidence that must be filled in; moving toward training and development management, education administration, training and development specialist, education consulting, or postsecondary teaching requires filling in each field's management, administrative, or licensing evidence.
Market signals and related directions for instructional coordinators: this page states only observations within the coverage of the sources.

US overall employment projection, not AI attribution | BLS/O*NET: 2025 employment about 248,700 people, 2025—2035 growth 2% (O*NET label 1%—2%, below average), average annual openings about 23,100; openings mainly include replacement from transfers and labor force exits. Insufficient evidence: occupation-level employment projections and national recruitment samples for instructional coordinators in China were not obtained, and individual hiring probability cannot be converted.

Employment outlook (BLS definition presented by O*NET, 2025—2035): growth below average (1%—2%), projected average annual openings about 23,100; openings include growth and replacement demand, do not equal net new jobs, and do not constitute an individual employment guarantee.

Transferable abilities | The shared foundations of adjacent directions include: curriculum and instruction analysis, instructional design and training, observation and evaluation, multi-party coordination and communication, and recording and documentation; but each path must fill in the tools, qualifications, and responsibility evidence corresponding to its new outputs and responsibilities.

Ability gaps | Moving toward adjacent directions such as training and development managers, education administrators (kindergarten through secondary), training and development specialists, educational/guidance and career counselors and advisors, or postsecondary teachers requires filling in the new position's management, administrative, licensing, or teaching and research evidence; adjacency is only for direction comparison and does not represent automatic transfer or qualification mutual recognition.

title.text: Instructional Coordinators occupational judgment: work, entry, and risk boundaries

subject.name: Instructional Coordinators
subject.summary: Instructional coordinators develop instructional material, coordinate educational content, and incorporate current technology into instruction to provide guidelines to educators and instructors for developing curricula and conducting courses; may train and coach teachers; includes educational consultants and specialists, and instructional material directors. The work includes analyzing curriculum standards and needs, designing instructional materials and training, observation and feedback, evaluation and iteration, and retrospective and recording. US wages and employment use the precise-occupation BLS 25-9031.00 definition presented by O*NET (2025 median annual wage 77,440 USD; 2024 employment about 232,600 people, 2024—2034 growth below average 1%—2%, projected average annual openings about 21,900, main industry educational services); the O*NET summary page does not list the 10/25/75/90 percentiles, and this page does not publish them; precise wages for this occupation in mainland China were not obtained and are registered as a visible gap.
